text: The prevalence of stress, anxiety, depression and burnout is quite high in medical students, and they differ in terms of personality traits and self-perception. The Big Five Model has embraced the idea of five basic personality traits: neuroticism, extroversion, conscientiousness, agreeableness, openness, and personality perceptions may be affected by stress. We aimed to test whether there are changes in the Five-Factor Model personality traits of medical students in response to anxiety and depression levels.
source_label: The impact of anxiety and depression levels on the Big Five personality traits
